messages.author: d4a835914e61fc5b
messages.subject: Repeated yearly visits
parts:
Hello unmarked group,

I have a large dataset that includes points that were visited multiple times across years (once per year, multiple years).  I know that accounting for this effort across years isn't possible in distsamp or gdistsamp, but is there a way that I can modify the confidence intervals ad-hoc to account for the fact that these points with multiple visits aren't independent points?  Or is there an alternative method to keep these points in the dataset instead of choosing one year's data and dropping the rest?

Thanks so much,
Sarah

messages.author: 4a15de51da4445ae
messages.subject: Re: [unmarked] Repeated yearly visits
parts:
hi Sarah,
 I think the gdistsamp() function will fit a model that is not unreasonable for that type of data. It doesn't allow for explicit population dynamics, but will definitely account for a certain type of within-site dependence.
regards,
andy

Hi Andy,
  I wonder if you could provide one last bit of clarity on this.  On a different post, I thought Richard suggested that gdistsamp cannot be used for repeated visits to sites across years:

https://groups.google.com/forum/?fromgroups=#!searchin/unmarked/gdistsamp/unmarked/w2_4lZkALzA/d934EipCpWMJ

Now I am wondering if he was remarking on something slightly different.  Is it fair to say that if we are not interested in temporal trends, but rather the effects of covariates on densities, we should be okay with gdistsamp if our survey design is to visit points once a year for multiple years?  When I read the manual I came away thinking that gdistsamp is designed for a closed population and thus annual variation in abundances might preclude its use.

messages.author: df74d6fccec2ff7e
messages.subject: Re: [unmarked] Repeated yearly visits
parts:
Hi Andrew,

I think I was trying to say that gdistsamp() will not directly estimate a trend parameter. But it can be used to abundance at various points in time. The thing to remember is that the model for abundance (N) is:

M(i) ~ Poisson(lambda), for i=1,...,nSites
N(i,t) ~ Binomial(M(i), phi) for t=1,...,nTimePeriods

The definition of "M(i)" and "phi" will depend upon the design, but basically, if phi=1, then abundance is not changing over time.

Richard
